subject: Manager spans & role alignment — proposal + comms
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Manager spans & role alignment — proposal + comms

Team —

I ran a quick alignment pass with the platform and runtime leads to address two recurring issues we raised in the last all-hands: uneven span-of-control across managers and blurry role scopes between Senior IC and Manager levels. The attached org-chart-v2.pdf is a proposition, plus a short comms draft (comm-plan-draft.docx). High level:

- Move infra-platform (8 ICs) under one manager and create a floating senior technical lead role to cover cross-service ops.
- Combine the small model-onboarding team (3 ICs) with runtime testing (4 ICs) under a single manager for Q3 to improve throughput.
- Formalize two Senior Staff IC slots (individual contributor promotion path) to reduce forced promotion-to-manager pressure.
- Average target span: 6–8 direct reports for production managers; where we increase spans we will add pairing leads and a 6‑week matrix reporting window to reduce risk.

Why now: we need clearer reporting before the mid-year performance calibration. If we don't clarify scope and reporting, promotion/comp conversations next quarter will be messy.

Ask: please review the attached and reply with two things by EOD Wednesday: 1) Scope concerns (teams or roles that will be negatively impacted), 2) Feedback on the comms plan and timing.

Sensitive note: this will touch compensation & promotion decisions. We should coordinate direct manager 1:1s before any all-hands comms; HR counsel will be required. I will forward to our external HR advisor for a quick legal/wording check.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake
VP Engineering, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: org-chart-v2.pdf (diagram), comm-plan-draft.docx (word draft)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Manager spans & role alignment — proposal + comms

Thanks Jordan — good work putting the options together. Quick thoughts:

- I like the two Senior Staff IC slots idea; it should help retain top talent who don’t want to manage.
- Concern: collapsing onboarding into runtime testing reduces dedicated discovery time — risk to onboarding SLAs for new customers. Can we add a measurable pulse (KPI) for onboarding 30/60/90 day targets?
- Promotions: we cannot run promotion calibrations until managers have clarity. Suggest we pause operational promotion decisions for two weeks while this lands.
- Comms: managers need a short FAQ to run 1:1s (template + talking points). Also propose the first manager sync be a private briefing, not a recorded all-hands.

Will add inline comments to the comm-plan doc. Looping HR (Carolyn) is good — please include a non-disparagement check on wording.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Operations
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com

Jordan —

Thanks for the forward. Reviewed the comm-plan-draft.docx and attached a redline (comm-template-redline.docx). High-level guidance:

- Keep initial messaging manager-facing only for 72 hours to allow 1:1s; do not send any org charts in the first manager briefing.
- Language: avoid implying comp/promotion guarantees. Use phrasing: "We are clarifying reporting lines and role scopes to improve career paths and operational effectiveness. Managers will share how these changes, if any, affect individual goals and timelines."
- Performance review tie-ins: do not retroactively change rating periods. Any promotion recommendations should be paused and re-evaluated in the next formal calibration window; exceptions require written justification and HR sign-off.
- Legal: ensure managers document 1:1 conversations (date + summary) for 6 months; provide a standard template.

Suggested timeline (high-level):
1) Tue–Thu (this week): private manager briefing + Q&A with HR present (30–45m).
2) Fri (end of week): managers complete 1:1 scheduling with direct reports.
3) Next Mon: managers begin 1:1s (no wider comms).
4) Two-week window: matrix reporting for overlap where needed; finalize org documentation at end of window.

I’m available for a 30‑minute call today at 4:30pm to walk through redlines.

Best,
Carolyn Dobson
Principal Consultant, Hirewell HR
carolyn@hirewell-hr.com

Attachments: comm-template-redline.docx
